The Asian Partnership for Peace (APP) talks have not been as successful as hoped by some, but still very fruitful, all things considered. India has declined membership status, however India and Pakistan both agreed to improve relations by respecting their de facto controlled zones in the Kashmir region. Along with this agreement, both countries are setting up a 15-mile wide demilitarized zone along this border. Reports have been made that Pakistan is respecting its side of the agreement and has already been pulilng its troops back.

Pakistan also agreed that it would not support any rebel factions in the Kasmir region, however it did so by making a follow-up comment that it won't take responsibility for individual actions. This language is seen as troubling to some political scholars who think that Pakistan should be more proactive in preventing such attacks from occuring in the first place.

While India and Pakistan may not yet be members of the APP, they have begun to improve their relations with one another. The Kashmir region DMZ is set to expire on January 21, 2020. If these two countries can trust each others boundaries after the DMZ is no longer in place is the big question, many in the international community are hoping so.
